prize_parts.citation: For the development of halide perovskites as solution-processable semiconductors for high-efficiency solar cells

statement.case_for: Halide perovskite absorbers are a materials-chemistry discovery in the full sense: a tunable ABX3 crystal family whose composition, dimensionality and defect chemistry can be designed, and which took certified solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to above 25% in roughly a decade. The structural chemistry is well characterised by diffraction and microscopy, the results are reproduced in laboratories worldwide, and the same materials now drive LEDs, detectors and tandem cells. Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park demonstrated the first efficient solid-state device, and Snaith's meso-superstructured and planar architectures opened the field to the many groups that followed. Of the shortlisted candidates it is the one that most clearly creates a new class of functional inorganic-hybrid materials, a theme the committee has recognised only occasionally in recent years.
statement.case_against: Credit is crowded: Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis made major contributions, and any three-person selection leaves out serious claims, including earlier work such as Kojima's. Operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, so a critic can argue that the technology has not yet proven itself outside the laboratory and that recognition would be premature. The opening ballots show that only Heiner Linke also placed it in the top four, and it has the narrowest support of the candidates I rank highly, so I do not claim that it commands a majority.

responses.point: Andrei Chabes ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first because it is mature and widely used, but notes that the 2010 cross-coupling prize may already cover part of this territory and that Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor.
responses.response: I agree that the maturity and independent confirmation are the strongest of any candidate on the list, and that the 2010 overlap is the main reservation. I would add that the Kosugi priority issue is only partly resolved by a two-name prize. Buchwald and Hartwig are secure on the general ligand-controlled method, but the committee would need to explain in the citation why this is not an extension of the 2010 award. That is why I keep it as an alternative rather than my first choice. If the committee prefers certainty on attribution and maturity over novelty of the materials class, I would accept B065.

responses.point: Heiner Linke ranks halide perovskites fourth, crediting the rapid efficiency gains and the link between materials chemistry, defect physics and device engineering, but regards stability and lead toxicity as leaving the long-term technology impact unsettled.
responses.response: That is a fair statement of the central doubt and I share it. My answer is that the prize would recognise the discovery of a new semiconductor family and the chemistry that made it work, not the commercial outcome. Tandem commercialisation is already under way, which is encouraging, but the scientific case does not depend on it. Linke's own preferred sequencing trio (B037) has a cleaner chemistry story and a more secure attribution, though; I would like to hear how he weighs the 1980 and 2002 sequencing-related prizes against it, since I cannot judge that overlap as well from my own field.

responses.point: Peter Brzezinski ranks targeted protein degradation first, as event-driven pharmacology with clinical-stage molecules, and chooses Crews, Deshaies and Handa to cover both the PROTAC and the cereblon glue strands.
responses.response: I agree that the concept is original and that the mechanism has been confirmed independently, so the science is mature even without an approved PROTAC. My difficulty is attribution and timing. The glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) and the PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) are separate achievements, and a single three-person citation either mixes them or omits major contributors. Taking Handa instead of Ciulli leaves out the person who supplied the structural basis for rational design. I would support B026 more readily as a two-part prize, for example one PROTAC part and one glue part, but the three-person cap makes that hard to realise.

responses.point: Peter Somfai places Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first, then photoredox catalysis, and argues that a two-person prize for Buchwald and Hartwig is fair and overdue.
responses.response: I accept that two names are defensible for B065 and that the recognition is arguably overdue. Where I differ is on the claim that the allocation is clean: Hartwig also appears in his C-H functionalisation trio, so the committee should be careful not to see the same laureates in two competing configurations. I would not choose photoredox as a second-best, because Somfai himself describes the credit as spread across Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi, with MacMillan already a laureate.

uncertainties: Whether perovskite stability and lead toxicity make recognition premature to a majority of the committee
Which three of Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Seok, Gratzel and Kanatzidis best represent the field, and how to treat Kojima, who is not among the credited names
Whether B065 should be preferred because of its maturity and secure attribution despite the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize
Whether the committee will accept targeted protein degradation as a single achievement, or would need a separate PROTAC and glue part
statement.conflict_note: No personal conflict is apparent for halide perovskites, Pd-catalysed C-N coupling or targeted protein degradation from my profile. Her field of electron crystallography and porous materials is close to the mesoporous silica (B068) and serial femtosecond crystallography (B007) candidates, which are not on this shortlist, and she is a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which is a professional rather than a scientific connection.
